name: Poltergeist Pinnacle

pitch_detail.notes: Face climbs a crisp dihedral just left of the pinnacle's granite shield, then traverses right ~40 ft across parallel dikes toward the face's edge; effectively unprotected for roughly the first 20 ft, ending in an insecure high-step/mantle crux below a small roof.
Corner/crack climbing up the lower face to a ledge system.
Ledge traverse through a short rock gully to gain the ridge crest.
Roughly 800 ft of ridge-crest climbing, typically simul-climbed or short-pitched, leading toward Mount Challenger's connecting ridge and true summit.

rappel_detail.pull: Short and plumb. Reports differ on the rope: some found a 30 m rope just enough, another needed most of a 40 m rope. Carry 40 m for margin.
rappel_detail.notes: One rappel down the summit pitch to the top of the 3rd-class scramble. Parties who prefer to downclimb the pitch skip it.
rappel_detail.anchor: old pitons plus a fixed cam or sling; check and back up
hazards: The anchor is weathered alpine hardware, not bolts. Inspect the slings before weighting them.
A moat just below the summit rocks may need a snow bridge to cross.
rappel_detail.station: Mount Challenger's summit block, at the top of the short 5.5-5.7 summit pitch.

rappels: 1 rappel on the descent, off Mount Challenger's summit block after traversing the ridge; no rappels on Poltergeist Pinnacle itself
descent_text: From the top of the technical climbing, simul-climb or belay short sections along the ridge crest (mostly low 5th class, up to 5.7) northward to Mount Challenger's main summit. From the true summit, descend the standard north-side Challenger Glacier route — the same line used for the peak's normal ascent — back down to Perfect Pass camp. Roped glacier travel is required; watch for crevasses, particularly late season as snow bridges deteriorate.
approach: Drive the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) east from Glacier about 12.5 miles and turn left onto the Hannegan Pass Road (FR 32), following it about 5 miles to the trailhead at its end; a Northwest Forest Pass is required to park. Hike the Hannegan Pass Trail about 4 miles to Hannegan Pass, drop into the Chilliwack River valley and cross the river, then climb onto Easy Ridge and follow its long, partly brushy climbers' path east. Cross the Imperfect Impasse, a moat-and-cliff notch that often needs a short low fifth-class downclimb, and climb snowfields to camp at Perfect Pass, roughly 16 miles and a full day from the car. From Perfect Pass, rope up, traverse around the Challenger Arm and cross about three miles of the crevassed Challenger Glacier to the base of the pinnacle. This is a genuine multi-day glacier expedition into one of the most remote, weather-exposed corners of the North Cascades, with essentially no bailout options once committed.
overview: East Face route on Poltergeist Pinnacle, the southernmost subsummit between Mount Challenger and Crooked Thumb in the Picket Range, approached via a glacier crossing to a dike-streaked granite shield. First climbed by Dan Aylward and Forrest Murphy, 2004.
beta: P1's crux follows a dihedral into wild face climbing across parallel dikes to the shield's edge, unprotectable for roughly 40 feet before cracks appear halfway up (5.9, rated R for the runout). P2-P3 ease onto cleaner, better-protected corner systems with a small roof at mid-height; the upper ~800ft relents to low-fifth-class buttress-crest terrain, typically simul-climbed to the summit.
gear: Single rack of cams (small to ~3 in)
Crampons and ice axe for glacier crossing
fa: Dan Aylward & Forrest Murphy, July 3-4, 2004 (East Face, new route)
